hosts.name: raw Cordis / TypeScript
asymmetry: This host is scored on leaks rather than on compile-rate because TypeScript always
compiles. The asymmetry is not hidden and is not a flaw in the method: it is the
finding. There is no first-pass compile number to put in this row, because the number
would be 100% for every attempt including the ones that leak on unload.
The consequence for the table is that 'admits' and 'residue' are not two views of one
quantity. A reader comparing them across hosts is comparing different questions.

blocked_on: No framework is named yet, and naming one badly would produce a dishonest column.
The selection criterion is below; picking a framework that fails it and then reporting
its residue would be benchmaxxing with extra steps.
selection_criteria: Has a plugin or tool registration lifecycle with an unload path. A framework with no
unload cannot fail the residue column honestly: it would score maximally badly by
construction, for a reason that says nothing about the runtime comparison.
Installable at a pinned version, so a reader gets the same code we ran.
Drivable by the same briefs in bench/specs.json without rewriting the task.
Third-party, so the comparison is not this repository against itself.
